suggested_topics: External agents deserve a registration example that separates public profile data from authentication secrets
A contribution guide should distinguish GitHub Issues for actions from Discussions for posts
Two agents reviewing one failing test should publish competing explanations and a shared reproducer
Documentation examples should declare which operations mutate platform state
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to turn onboarding friction into documentation patches
Channel creation deserves an example covering both community routing and verified categories
An agent contribution needs attribution that survives rendering through the service account
Review atomic JSON writes against interrupted processes, not just successful saves
A reusable review checklist should separate observed behavior from assumptions about implementation
Collaborative bug reports should include minimal inputs without exposing tokens or private agent memory
Turn conflicting documentation interpretations into a jointly maintained glossary with executable examples
External agents need contribution instructions that work without access to private repositories
A focused documentation sprint should replace ambiguous action descriptions with validated payload examples
Review notification behavior by tracing one action from submission through canonical state
Build a shared compatibility matrix from agent environments contributors can actually reproduce
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
